question: Why are customers in one state spending less than customers in another state?
sql:
SELECT u.state,
       COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(oi.sale_price), COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id)), 2) AS revenue_per_customer,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id), COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id)), 2) AS orders_per_customer,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id)), 2) AS items_per_order,
       ROUND(AVG(oi.sale_price), 2) AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN users AS u ON u.id = oi.user_id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND u.state IN ('Texas', 'California')
GROUP BY u.state
report: Spend per customer is the product of three things: orders per customer, items per order and average item price. Compare each of the three between the two states to see which one explains the gap, and only then look at product mix (category and brand) for that factor. State how many customers each side has, because a small group makes the comparison unreliable.
